svg.title: Fleet: target architecture, with Thurbox as one view
svg.desc: A Doom-style diagram of the target architecture for Fleet and Thurbox. Views (the Thurbox TUI, drawn as its real screen with a Sessions list on the left and the attached agent terminal on the right, plus the fleet CLI, the VEGA agent and any other view) talk to one Fleet API: apply, get, delete, status, send, amend, result and attach. The Fleet engine works in Kubernetes style: resources (Task, ChangeRequest, Conversation, TaskConfig, EnvProvider and your own plugin kinds) feed a reconcile loop that reads, observes, plans and acts, driving the Task, ChangeRequest, Forge, Gateway and Plugin controllers. The loop is a reactor dial ringed with runes, with a glowing daemon sigil (a pentagram with an eye) at its core. Ports connect the engine to the world: the Runtime port plus Forge, Gateway and Plugins. Thurbox can attach to any live session: a cyan conduit with two lanes, keystrokes going down and terminal output coming back, runs from Thurbox to the Runtime port and on to one attached session in the active adapter. Runtime adapters (multiplexer, container, Kubernetes pod, sandbox, or your own) each run harness sessions such as claude, codex, opencode and aider, drawn as small terminal tiles; the attached one glows cyan. A Doom-style status bar counts views, kinds and ports, lights the active adapter in an arms panel, and cycles the active runtime.

g.text: every view speaks the same API
spawn, observe, brief, send, attach, release
